title: Iman Gadzhi on building an intentional micro personal brand and monetizing it with coaching first
summary: Iman walks through a five-step playbook: build an intentional personal brand, keep it micro-niche, run a content strategy, monetize with information (coaching first), then scale into group coaching and digital products. He argues audience quality beats size and that a personal brand lets bootstrapped founders attract customers instead of chasing them.

principles.text: A personal brand is the bootstrapper's equalizer: it replaces VC money and paid acquisition as your distribution.
principles.quote: if you're trying to bootstrap your businesses a personal brand is the best it's basically like the great equalizer okay it basically means that now you can actually compete against all these industries

principles.text: Optimize for audience quality and revenue per follower, not follower count.
principles.quote: audience quality is much more important than audience size your follower account doesn't not matter what matters is how much each follower is worth to you

principles.text: You don't need to be an expert, only one step ahead of your audience; too far ahead becomes unrelatable.
principles.quote: you do not need to be an expert you just need to be one step ahead of someone else

principles.text: Start monetizing information with one-on-one coaching to validate the offer and learn the market before building courses.
principles.quote: the best way to monetize your brand at the beginning is through coaching coaching is direct personal and gives you the ability to validate your offer and understand your market

principles.text: Tell the wrong customers to stay away; it sharpens your audience and your offer.
principles.quote: if you're making less than 250,000 a year in your business just please don't watch it because it is genely true I will confuse you more than I'll help you

principles.text: Don't pick a broad niche; corner a small unique value zone inside it.
principles.quote: I don't even think you should find your Niche you should find your unique value Zone okay the little small aspect of the market that you're cornering
